summary: This bill amends title 10 of the U.S. Code to bar excluding Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, or Space Force members from any occupational specialty, career field, or assignment based on gender, updates the 1994 NDAA to require gender-neutral occupational standards based on rigorous, performance-predictive criteria covering technical, tactical, cognitive, and physical abilities, lengthens congressional review periods for proposed changes, and requires submission of an unredacted Institute for Defense Analyses study plus a Comptroller General review.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends military personnel policies regarding gender-neutral occupational standards and assignments. It contains no provisions related to funding levels, appropriations, or government expenditures of any kind.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection mechanisms.
The bill addresses military assignment standards and does not engage with healthcare delivery, coverage, or insurance systems.
No provisions in the bill relate to firearms regulation, ownership, or military weapons policies.
The bill is silent on immigration, border policy, or pathways to citizenship.
No language in the bill addresses reproductive rights or abortion access.
While the bill amends Title 10 and NDAA provisions concerning Armed Forces standards, it does not alter funding levels, procurement, or overall defense spending.
The bill contains no environmental, regulatory, or climate-related provisions.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net programs.
The bill does not address schools, education funding, or school choice policies.
No content relates to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The bill does not modify sentencing, policing, or criminal justice procedures.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are present.
The bill does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.

The bill focuses on codifying gender-neutral military occupational standards and prohibiting gender-based exclusions from assignments. It does not reference sexual orientation, gender identity, or broader LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No provisions concern foreign assistance or international aid.
The bill does not engage with voting rights, election procedures, or voter access.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance provisions exist.
The bill does not address union rights, worker protections, or labor relations.
The bill establishes anti-discrimination rules for military assignments based on gender but does not address religious exemptions or conflicts between religious liberty and civil rights.
